section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-16 is where an LLM writes code. It is one of the three places an LLM appears in the factory (with N-17 and N-19; ../../dag.md#7-rules-every-node-obeys rule 5). The worker implements exactly one ticket inside its declared files in the workspace N-14 gave it, and its turn ends at a commit on the ticket's branch. Everything mechanical after that commit (push, pull request, record) is code in the launcher's post step, so a worker never runs git push, gh pr create or event.sh, and the pr.opened record is written only after code has checked that the pull request exists at the claimed head (rebuild/investigation/L13-llms-doing-scheduler-work.md#7-decisions-an-llm-makes-that-a-rule-could-make D22).

The worker's verdict comes later from a status it can read and cannot edit: coq/gate on the head sha (D05) and the reviewer's record (N-19). The worker never tests in a pane and never waits for a result: it runs the ticket's host-runnable acceptance commands itself, commits, and ends; the pods run the suites (D22; rebuild/investigation/L11-governance-layer.md#52-findings-f1-to-f18 F13 is the polling this ends).

section.title: Input: the worker brief inside a seat run
section.text: The brief is bundle_dir/brief.md rendered by N-13 from the ticket record (D04: the ticket is a record in the store, never a file on a branch). Its sections, in order:
section.field: id and full title, the parent epic id and title when one exists, the DAG node the ticket was cut from (anchor into this book).
the input record that starts the ticket and the output record that ends it, as declared at cut (D16).
the declared files; the fence of the bundle allows writes only there (N-13).
every acceptance command with its observed exit code on main (N-18) and the exit the ticket expects after the change, and where it runs (host or pod).
the ticket's numbered steps and its degrees of freedom; the only choices the worker makes are the ones the ticket names (roles/worker.json must line 2, carried forward).

the few that are judgement, not fence: a breadcrumb comment at the fix site with what broke, why it mattered, why this fix, what it costs (global rule); no em dash; UTC; one concern; the structured output contract below.
on attempt n+1, the failure record verbatim: review.changes observations, merge.conflict detail, the prior seat.result's blocked reason, or the gate's failing suite with its log link.
stated once as information: max turns, budget, wall clock, stall, with "the launcher enforces these".
section.text: The workspace is cwd, on branch wo/<ticket> at origin/main (attempt 1) or at origin/wo/<ticket> (attempt n+1), clean.

section.title: Output record: pr.opened, or phase.failed
section.text: The seat's structured output, worker.result (record.schema.json#/$defs/worker.result): ready with commit_sha, summary, evidence per criterion and files_changed, or blocked with reason, observations and repro.

pr.opened (record.schema.json#/$defs/pr.opened), code 100, on the shared committed envelope, written by the close-out only after the PR is read back at the pushed head: ticket, run_id, attempt, lease, repo, base_ref main, head_repo, source seat, branch, pr, head_sha, base_sha, files, evidence, url, effects. It is also N-23's input shape. Same Commit: tickets.transition in_flight to pr_open (../../shared/contracts.xml#ticket-transitions), Lease.Release, and run:RUN_ID to closed_out with phase_record_ref.

phase.failed (../N-15/record.schema.json#/$defs/phase.failed, node N-16) carries failure_body: after a diff check refusal it is failure_kind output_rejected with step diff_check (the seat.result is already committed and records are append-only, so the refusal is its own record); after three failed close-out passes it is failure_kind phase.failed. N-11 charges either once with session new.

section.title: Mechanism: the brief, the run, the close-out by code
section.mermaid: flowchart LR B[bundle brief.md plus workspace on wo/ticket] --> R[claude -p run: edit inside declared files, run host acceptance, commit] R --> O{structured output worker.result} O -- ready --> C[close-out in the service: diff check, effects intent, push, PR find or create, read back, pr.opened 100] O -- blocked --> X[seat.result 423 seat_blocked, from N-15] C -- diff check fails --> Y[phase.failed output_rejected] C -- three failed passes --> Z[phase.failed 500; the slot keeps the commit]
section.step: The run. The worker reads the brief and the files it names; it edits only inside them (a write outside is a recorded permission denial, not a prompt); it runs the acceptance commands marked host (lint, unit tests runnable without the cluster) through the repository's make targets; it fixes until they pass or until its limits end the run; it commits with the message "<ticket id> - <title>" plus a body naming the breadcrumb; it returns worker.result. A worker that cannot finish inside its files returns blocked with observations (path, line, saw, expected) and a repro command; a blocked output with no observation is refused by the launcher as output_rejected no_observations (kickback without evidence is prose, specs/SPEC-03-dag-and-node-contract.xml#s-records).

The fence (N-13) and the slot ACL (N-14): Write and Edit only under the declared files; Bash allows make *, the acceptance commands, and git status|diff|log|add|commit|rev-parse|branch --show-current; git push, gh, podman, herdr, treehouse and rm -rf outside the workspace are denied. make targets that would touch the cluster are not allowed in the worker's Bash list; the pods run them.

Commit identity: user.name and user.email come from the mirror's config that N-14 sets (seats.json git identity); the environment holds nothing else (../../shared/seat-contract.xml#launch-flags); the session trailer is rendered into the commit template by N-13, never typed by the worker (L11 F14).

section.title: Close-out: outbox push and pull request, pr.opened
section.text: Function closeout(run) in scheduler/internal/closeout/worker.go, run in the service as principal coq-svc acting as N-16 (../../shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix row forge-pr), level-triggered on run entities in result_committed with a done worker seat.result. The seat never pushes and never calls the forge. Every step is idempotent, and every Commit carries the worker lease.
section.step: Diff check, in the service against the slot's worktree: git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD; every path inside the ticket's live claims (../../shared/contracts.xml#claims), none an aggregate or runtime file; HEAD equals worker.result.commit_sha; the tree is clean. A failure is phase.failed step diff_check with failure_kind output_rejected and the stray paths; no push happens.

Decide. One Commit with key N-16/branch.push/TICKET@HEAD_SHA/r1 writing two effects rows in state intent (../../shared/contracts.xml#outbox): the push of wo/TICKET at HEAD_SHA (provider github, action branch.push) and the PR open (action pr.open, op id N-16/pr.open/TICKET@ATTEMPT/r1). Nothing calls GitHub before this Commit.

Push. git push from the mirror with forge-pr (never --force); effects.advance intent to sent to accepted; read back the remote head of wo/TICKET; equal to HEAD_SHA is done. A non-fast-forward rejection is phase.failed step branch.push reason push_rejected and a defect record, because fencing should have prevented a second writer.

Pull request. Look up an open PR by head branch first (the outbox lookup key); reuse it, else create it with base main, title the ticket id and full title, and the summary and evidence table as body; effects.advance to accepted.

Read back and record. GET the PR: head sha equals HEAD_SHA and state open. Then one Commit with key N-16/pr.open/TICKET@ATTEMPT/r1: effects.advance pr.open to done, the pr.opened record, tickets.transition in_flight to pr_open, Lease.Release, run:RUN_ID to closed_out with phase_record_ref. No record claims the PR before this read back.
section.text: The branch stays in the slot until N-45 releases it on merge or dead; nothing else holds wo/TICKET because every workspace is its own worktree (memory release-branch-before-pr-opened).

section.title: Rework on attempt n+1
section.text: review.changes, gate.red and merge.conflict (including a branch behind main) are failures N-11 charges to the worker phase, attempt n plus 1, session resume-if-done (../../shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner). N-14 cuts the workspace from origin/wo/TICKET; N-13 renders the brief with the failure records verbatim and the session the attempt names. The worker fixes, and for a merge.conflict or behind it merges origin/main into wo/TICKET and resolves inside its files; the close-out pushes the same branch and reuses the PR; a new head sha starts a new gate and a new review.

A conflict outside the declared files is a scheduling defect (memory one-file-one-in-flight-ticket): the worker returns blocked conflict_outside_files, N-11 charges it, and the dead card after the third says so.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: A worker exists only inside an N-15 run started from a dispatch; the close-out is a service controller level-triggered on run entities. No person and no agent starts, wakes, nudges or ends a worker.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: the unit's RuntimeMaxSec (run.deadline_seconds.worker) and N-12's stall bound (stall.seconds.worker), ../../shared/contracts.xml#timing
wait.fallback: the run ends blocked; N-11 charges it

wait.attempts: 3 passes, backoff 5 s, 15 s, 45 s; an unknown outcome is looked up by the remote head before any resend
wait.fallback: phase.failed step branch.push; the commit stays in the slot

wait.what: the forge PR lookup, create and read back
wait.attempts: 3 passes; lookup by head branch before any create

wait.fallback: the next pass resends the same key; a replay is harmless

wait.attempts: renewed by the close-out while it works
wait.fallback: a 412 lease_not_current stops the close-out; N-12 and N-11 handle the expiry

section.text: The worker never waits for the gate, the reviewer or the merge.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: Inner layer: the close-out recovery in code, three passes, no model (../../shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner row phase.failed). After the third failed pass, phase.failed with failure_body (failure_kind phase.failed, passes 3) goes to N-11, which charges once with session new. A diff_check refusal is not retried: it is phase.failed with failure_kind output_rejected at once. Outer layer: N-11's three worker attempts, then dead and one card.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many workers run at once, one per ticket, each in its own slot and branch; claims are disjoint (N-03) and the slot ACL plus the fence deny writes elsewhere.
Two workers on one ticket: impossible past GrantDispatch; a stale run cannot Commit (412), and a non-fast-forward push catches the last case.

Main moves while the worker works: the merge (N-09) either merges the PR or returns merge.conflict (or behind) as a failure; N-11 sends it back to the worker as attempt n plus 1. N-09 never rebases a branch itself.
The reviewer and a rework worker at one head: the reviewer is detached at its dispatched head; a new push is a new head with its own gate and review.
Two close-out passes for one run: both use the same operation keys; the effects rows are looked up before any resend; pr.opened is one Commit.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: The PR exists at the head sha, read back. Acts: N-23 plans the suites; N-48 when the diff touches an owner surface; N-07 grants the reviewer and gate phases on pr_open.
Close-out failed three passes, or the diff check refused. Acts: N-11 charges once.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: argv and results of the diff check, push and forge calls (no token)

path.retention: until merge or dead; never a branch with an open pull request

section.text: The slot is N-14's path. Nothing is written into the repository on main by this node; the pull request is the only path.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The worker seat (N-13): writes only inside its claims in its rwX slot; Bash make, the acceptance commands and git read and commit verbs; denied git push, gh, podman, herdr, treehouse, Agent, Task. No forge credential, no network but the Anthropic API.

The close-out: principal coq-svc acting as N-16; credential forge-pr from STATE/secrets (../../shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix), used only for the push and the PR; effects rows and the Commits above. No cluster access.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/closeout -run TestStrayFile: a change outside the claims yields phase.failed step diff_check, failure_kind output_rejected, and no effects row

section.item: The diff check refuses a stray path before any effect.

item.proof: go test TestOutboxBeforeForge: a fake forge records no call before the branch.push Commit; a crash after the push leaves the effect unknown and the next pass looks up the remote head before resending

section.item: No forge call before the intent Commit.

item.proof: go test TestCloseoutIdempotent: two passes yield one push, one PR, one pr.opened
go test TestReadBackBeforeRecord: a fake forge returning another head yields phase.failed step pr.verify and no pr.opened
go test TestPrOpenedIsN23Input: every pr.opened example validates against ../N-23/record.schema.json#/$defs/input
host probe: a worker seat running git push or gh is denied and the close-out still opens the PR as coq-svc

section.item: The seat cannot push; the service does.

item.proof: go test TestThreePassesThenN11: three failed pushes yield one phase.failed with passes 3 and one N-11 attempt

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: workers_done, workers_blocked_by_reason, prs_opened, closeout_failed, rework_attempts_by_number (1, 2, 3), cost_usd by ticket. The Machine screen (N-39) for N-16 shows live workers with ticket, attempt, progress age and cost; the Stats screen (N-40) shows pull requests opened per hour and the attempt histogram; the Alerts screen (N-41) shows push_rejected and conflict_outside_files because both are scheduling defects.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a worker's work: the PR on GitHub (title is the ticket id and title); ctl run RUN_ID for the run entity, seat.result and effects rows; the close-out log for the push and forge steps.

A phase.failed on push or PR: the effects rows say which step and whether the outcome was unknown; nothing is lost because the commit is in the slot. Never push a worker's branch by hand: a hand push makes the next close-out non-fast-forward and a defect.
A dead ticket after three charged failures: the card (N-28) carries the reasons and the last observations; the owner's options are re-cut, split or cancel.
Cleanup: the close-out log by cleanup-seat-runs.sh, the slot by cleanup-workspaces.sh (N-14), the branch by cleanup-branches.sh (N-45); all dry-run first and registered.

edge.record: seat.result done for a worker run (the brief ran inside the launcher's unit)

attempt n+1 after review.changes, merge.conflict or a red gate: ticket retry_wait to ready, then a new grant (../../dag.md#4-re-entries)
